Method of Attack: Distributed via phishing emails with malicious Word or Excel attachments or links
Use of document templates that prompt users to enable macros by clicking 'Enable Content' or 'Enable Editing'
Malicious attachments contain macros that install malware when enabled
Spam campaigns pretending to be invoices, invites, payment, shipping information, eFaxes, voicemails, and more
Use of fake Google Docs or Google Sheets links to download executables (BazarLoader)
Stealing passwords, providing remote access, and downloading additional modules (Dridex, QakBot)
Partnering with ransomware payloads (Ryuk, Conti, ProLock)
Use of stylized or warning document templates to trick users into enabling macros
Impacted Systems: Microsoft Office Word and Excel users
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious attachments or links
Malicious Word and Excel documents with embedded macros
Links to fake Google Docs or Sheets documents
Indicators of Compromise: Emails containing malicious Word or Excel attachments
Links to fake Google Docs or Google Sheets documents
Attachments prompting to click 'Enable Content' or 'Enable Editing'
Document templates mimicking invoices, shipping info, DocuSign, Microsoft Defender, Word update screens
